newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids steady to up with crude, gas.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids steady to up with crude, gas.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices were unchanged to up slightly Monday in lackluster trade, boosted by another rally in crude and natural gas though mild East Coast weather this week should temper the bulls.

"I was looking for lower (resid) numbers, but if crude stays above $20 (a barrel) and gas continues up, resid will be more competitive and prices could move up," said one East Coast utility source, adding further gains in city gate gas prices should trigger more fuel switching to resid.
But few saw any surge in prices near-term, with eastern weather mostly expected to remain below-seasonal this week, then warm slightly by the weekend.

In New York Harbor, physical one percent edged up slightly to $16 a barrel, with September one percent paper talked a quarter higher at $16.25-50 with firmer crude. Oct paper was quoted at $16.40-70, while Q4 was pegged on either side of $17.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour, still well supported by an 850,000-barrel New York utility August buy program, jumped more than a quarter to about $18, traders said.
High sulphurs in New York mostly were unchanged.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent was stable at $15.50-75, while three percent firmed slightly to $14.75.
Traders reported a one percent cargo sale to a Florida utility in the $16.40-80 area (delivered).

New York city gate gas prices eased slightly to the low-$2.40s/mmBtu, or $15.31 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, firmed a couple of cents to the $2.25/mmBtu area, or $14.18 a barrel.
